close_reason: Resolved together: all 6 FileNode/* handlers now consult supports_type::<FileNode>() at the top and return accountNotSupportedByMethod when the backend has opted out. Mirrors canonical jmap-mail-server snippet.rs:35 pattern. Regression test all_handlers_gate_on_supports_type_false uses a NoFileNodeBackend wrapper (mirroring NoSnippetBackend in mail-server tests/integration.rs:490).
description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:69-72; called from
nowhere in the crate.

```rust
/// Returns `true` if this account supports the given JMAP object
/// type. Backends that support all types unconditionally can always
/// return `true`.
fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool;
```

Every implementor of `FileNodeBackend` is forced to write a method
that no handler in this crate ever calls. `grep` for `supports_type`
across `src/` only finds the trait definition and the two test-double
impls (lib.rs:399, memory.rs:565) — both of which return `true`
trivially. No `handle_filenode_*` consults it.

Compare canonical sibling `jmap-mail-server`: its handler
`snippet.rs:35` actually calls `backend.supports_type::<SearchSnippet>()`
to short-circuit when the backend has opted out of the type. There
is precedent for `supports_type` mattering — but only on the canonical
side.

Two consequences for the API contract:

1. **Defensive-code-forcing.** Every FileNodeBackend implementor (in
   stoa, kith, downstream consumers) writes `fn supports_type<O>(&self)
   -> bool { true }`. That boilerplate buys nothing because the handler
   library does not consult the result. Forever-pub method, forever-
   boilerplate cost.

2. **Divergence from canonical.** The canonical extension-server
   template uses this method to gate handlers; filenode-server does
   not. If a future caller adds a second JMAP object type to the
   FileNode capability (the draft has not, but the spec could evolve)
   and adds the gate-check pattern from `snippet.rs`, the existing
   backends will continue to return `true` and the gate will be a
   no-op.

Pick one:

- If FileNode is the only type that will ever live under this trait,
  remove `supports_type` from the trait. Saves implementor work and
  removes a method whose only documented purpose ("Called by the
  server consumer e.g. the session capability builder") is also not
  exercised by any code path in this crate.

- If the gate is intended for future extension, then
  `register_filenode_handlers` (lib.rs:75) should call
  `supports_type::<FileNode>()` once and either panic / return Err
  on `false`, or each handler should early-exit with `unknownMethod`
  on `false`. Pick the early-exit pattern that matches `snippet.rs`
  in the canonical sibling.

This is api-contract because every consumer pays the boilerplate
tax and depends on a documented method that the library does not
honor. Either honor it or remove it.
title: FileNodeBackend::supports_type<O> is part of the trait contract but never called by this crate's handlers
